Charles Perrault’s version (first published version of the tale)

Charles Perrault was a French author in the 17th century. He laid the foundations for a new literary genre, the fairy tale, with his works derived from pre-existing folk tales. The best known of his tales include ʼLe Petit Chaperon rougeʼ (Little Red Riding Hood), ʼCendrillonʼ (Cinderella), ʼLe Chat Bottéʼ (Puss in Boots) and ʼLa Barbe bleueʼ (Bluebeard). Many of Perrault’s stories were rewritten by the Brothers Grimm, continue to be printed and have been adapted to opera, ballet (such as Tchaikovsky’s The Sleeping Beauty), theatre, and film (Disney).

The story had as its subject an “attractive, well-bred young lady”, a village girl of the country being deceived into giving a wolf she encountered the information he needed to find her grandmother’s and eat the old woman while at the same time avoiding being noticed by woodcutters. Then he proceeded to lay a trap for the Red Riding Hood who ends up being asked to climb into the bed before being eaten by the wolf, where the story ends. The wolf emerges the victor of the encounter and there is no happy ending.

Charles Perrault explained the ‘moral’ at the end so that no doubt is left to his intended meaning:

From this story one learns that children, especially young lasses, pretty, courteous and well-bred, do very wrong to listen to strangers, And it is not an unheard thing if the Wolf is thereby provided with his dinner. I say Wolf, for all wolves are not of the same sort; there is one kind with an amenable disposition – neither noisy, nor hateful, nor angry, but tame, obliging and gentle, following the young maids in the streets, even into their homes.

Alas! Who does not know that these gentle wolves are of all such creatures the most dangerous!

December 6

15 And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it. (Colossians 2:15 KJV)

This is speaking of when Jesus went to heaven and defeated the devil and his demons (Revelation 12:9), and spoiled them, which means He striped them of all their power, and paraded them as defeated foes. The devil now has no power at all, but the church seems to have missed the show, and many teach that the devil has great power to defeat us, which is just not so. The only power the devil has is to deceive us with his lies, and then if we yield to him, we give him our power to use against us. The principalities and powers are referring to all the evil spirits that are used by the devil, and they all have been stripped of all their power. Does this mean that we don’t have to worry about the devil and his wiles? No, the devil is still dangerous, and can cause us harm, but only if we fall for his deceptions and lies. He can only hurt us if we let him, as he has no power of his own.

If the Christian could just realize that the devil can only deceive us, and if we don’t fall for his lies, then he has no way to harm us, and he will flee from us if we are serving God and will rebuke him in the name of Jesus (James 4:7). The devil and all demons have been placed under the feet of Jesus body (the church), and if you are a Christian, you have your foot on the devils head, and can stomp him when he tries to bother you, or bring sickness on you. You don’t have to be afraid of the devil, but you sure have to be wary of his lies and temptations, as he is the father of all lies (John 8:44). If we would just realize how the devil has been stripped of any power he had, then we would have no reason to be concerned about his overcoming us. If we do yield ourselves to the devil through sin, then he has the right to hit us with sickness, poverty, death, etc., so we must not live in sin and give him the opportunity to kill, steal and destroy us (John 10:10). Thank you Jesus for giving us dominion over the devil and his demons!
